# Crash Course: Agentic Engineering — Capstone

Фінальний проєкт курсу **fwdays · Crash Course: Agentic Engineering** (вересень 2026).

Слайди курсу: <https://koldovsky.github.io/2026-agentic-engineering-crash-course/>
Демо-репозиторії занять: [`…-day01`](https://github.com/koldovsky/2026-agentic-engineering-crash-course-day01) · [`…-day02`](https://github.com/koldovsky/2026-agentic-engineering-crash-course-day02)

## Що зробити

**Побудуй невеликий власний проєкт** — будь-який, який тобі цікавий.

Стек вільний: Next.js, Python, Go, Rust, мобільний застосунок, CLI, бот — на твій вибір.

**Масштаб скромний.** Краще маленький проєкт, проведений через повний інженерний цикл, ніж великий
«наче працює».

**Застосуй практики Agentic Engineering з курсу** — стільки, скільки доречно для твого проєкту:

- **контекст-інженерія** — правила / `AGENTS.md`, статичний vs динамічний контекст;
- **цикли (loop engineering)** — замість ручного покрокового промптингу;
- **верифікація** — тести / evals / перевірки замість «здається, працює»;
- **maker ≠ checker** — окремий агент або прохід на рев'ю;
- **специфікації наперед (SDD)** — якщо доречно.

**Project Factory** — за бажанням, не обов'язково (хочеш повну фабрику — запусти
`/project-factory:init` у себе).

**Запиши відео-демо на 1–2 хвилини:** коротко покажи продукт і розкажи, як саме ти будував(ла) його
агентно.

> Рівень глибини обираєш ти. Не оцінюється ні обсяг коду, ні кількість застосованих практик.
> Оцінюється те, що практики **справді є** і що кожна з них **коректно доведена** — на неї можна
> подивитися: файл, коміт, тест, прогін, запис.

## Як здати

**1. Зроби fork цього репозиторію** — разом із ним приїде шаблон PR.

```bash
gh repo fork koldovsky/2026-agentic-engineering-crash-course-capstone --clone
```

**2. Поклади свій проєкт у форк на окрему гілку** (будь-яким стеком).

```bash
cd 2026-agentic-engineering-crash-course-capstone
git checkout -b <твоє-ім'я>
```

Файли курсу в корені (`README.md`, `RUBRIC.md`, `.github/`) не чіпай — просто додай свій проєкт
поруч. Найзручніше покласти його в окрему теку, наприклад `submissions/<твоє-ім'я>/`: так у diff
видно рівно твою роботу.

Якщо зручніше тримати код в **окремому репозиторії** — тримай, і додай на нього посилання в описі PR.
У такому разі гілка у форку може містити лише короткий `README.md` із посиланням.

**3. Відкрий Pull Request і заповни шаблон:**

- **Ім'я** (справжнє — воно піде в сертифікат);
- **посилання на відео-демо** (1–2 хв);
- **опис застосованих практик Agentic Engineering** — що саме ти робив(ла) агентно, які інструменти /
  MCP використав(ла), що вирішував(ла) ти, а що агент.

PR може лишатися відкритим — зливати його не треба.

Що саме вважається доказом для кожної практики — **[RUBRIC.md](./RUBRIC.md)**.
Сертифікат — після прийнятого capstone. Дедлайн оголошується в чаті курсу (fwdays).

| Файл | Навіщо |

| [`RUBRIC.md`](./RUBRIC.md) | що приймається і що вважається доказом для кожної практики |
| [`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md`](./.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md) | GitHub підставить його у твій PR — заповнюєш і здаєш |

content.text:
### Run openspec init non-interactively with specific tools

Source: https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec/blob/main/docs/troubleshooting.md

Use this to configure AI tools during init without prompts. Replace 'claude,cursor' with a comma-separated list of tool IDs, or use '--tools all' for everything or '--tools none' to skip tool setup.

```bash
openspec init --tools claude,cursor
```

--------------------------------

### openspec init usage examples

Source: https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec/blob/main/docs-lab/reference/cli.md

Shows three ways to run openspec init: with no options for an interactive tool picker, with --tools to specify tools non-interactively, and with --tools none to create only the openspec/ structure.

```bash
openspec init                        # current directory, interactive tool picker
```

```bash
openspec init --tools claude,cursor  # set up specific tools, no prompts
```

```bash
openspec init --tools none           # openspec/ structure only, no tool files
```

--------------------------------

### Initialize OpenSpec in an existing project with openspec init

Source: https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec/blob/main/docs/existing-projects.md

Run in the terminal to initialize OpenSpec in an existing project. The `openspec init` command creates the `openspec/` directory and adds your AI tool's commands.

```bash
$ cd your-existing-project
$ openspec init          # adds openspec/ and your AI tool's commands
```

--------------------------------

### Directory structure created by openspec init

Source: https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec/blob/main/docs/cli.md

Shows the folder structure and tool configuration files generated by the init command.

```text
openspec/
├── specs/              # Your specifications (source of truth)
├── changes/            # Proposed changes
└── config.yaml         # Project configuration

.claude/skills/         # Claude Code skills (if claude selected)
.cursor/skills/         # Cursor skills (if cursor selected)
.cursor/commands/       # Cursor OPSX commands (if delivery includes commands)
.agents/skills/         # Shared skills for AGENTS.md-compatible tools (if agents selected)
... (other tool configs)

```

### openspec init > Output

Source: https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec/blob/main/docs-lab/reference/cli.md

**Output**

Each selected tool gets OpenSpec's skills and commands in its own directory:

```
▌ OpenSpec structure created
✔ Setup complete for Claude Code

OpenSpec Setup Complete

Created: Claude Code
6 skills and 6 commands in .claude/
Config: openspec/config.yaml (schema: spec-driven)

Getting started:
  Start your first change: /opsx:propose "your idea"

Restart your IDE for the new commands to take effect.
```

`--tools none` creates only `openspec/config.yaml`. On an already-initialized project, init rewrites the installed files in place and the summary reads `Refreshed: Claude Code` with `Config: openspec/config.yaml (exists)`.

### Project configuration example (openspec/config.yaml)

Source: https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec/blob/main/docs/opsx.md

Example project configuration file at `openspec/config.yaml`. Sets the default schema, injects project context into all artifact instructions, and defines per-artifact rules. Context is limited to 50KB and rules are only injected for matching artifacts.

```yaml
# openspec/config.yaml
schema: spec-driven

context: |
  Tech stack: TypeScript, React, Node.js
  API conventions: RESTful, JSON responses
  Testing: Vitest for unit tests, Playwright for e2e
  Style: ESLint with Prettier, strict TypeScript

rules:
  proposal:
    - Include rollback plan
    - Identify affected teams
  specs:
    - Use Given/When/Then format for scenarios
  design:
    - Include sequence diagrams for complex flows
```

--------------------------------

### config.yaml structure for OPSX config

Source: https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec/blob/main/docs/migration-guide.md

Example of the config.yaml structure for the new config system. It defines the default schema, optional project context (max 50KB), and per-artifact rules for proposal, specs, design, and tasks.

```yaml
# Required: Default schema for new changes
schema: spec-driven

# Optional: Project context (max 50KB)
# Injected into ALL artifact instructions
context: |
  Your project background, tech stack,
  conventions, and constraints.

# Optional: Per-artifact rules
# Only injected into matching artifacts
rules:
  proposal:
    - Include rollback plan
  specs:
    - Use Given/When/Then format
  design:
    - Document fallback strategies
  tasks:
    - Break into 2-hour maximum chunks
```

--------------------------------

### Configure openspec/config.yaml manually

Source: https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec/blob/main/docs/customization.md

Manual example of the openspec/config.yaml file. It sets a default schema, injects project context, adds per-artifact rules, per-operation guidance, and the GitHub Copilot cloud agent opt-in. The githubCopilot.cloudAgent key is set by openspec init and controls whether init/update generate its files.

```yaml
# openspec/config.yaml
schema: spec-driven

context: |
  Tech stack: TypeScript, React, Node.js, PostgreSQL
  API style: RESTful, documented in docs/api.md
  Testing: Jest + React Testing Library
  We value backwards compatibility for all public APIs

rules:
  proposal:
    - Include rollback plan
    - Identify affected teams
  specs:
    - Use Given/When/Then format
    - Reference existing patterns before inventing new ones

operations:
  apply:
    guidance:
      - Run focused tests before the full suite
  archive:
    guidance:
      - Keep the completion summary concise

# Set by `openspec init` when you choose (or decline) the GitHub Copilot
# cloud coding agent; controls whether `init`/`update` generate its files.
githubCopilot:
  cloudAgent: false
```

--------------------------------

### Full example config.yaml

Source: https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec/blob/main/docs-lab/reference/configuration/config-yaml.md

A filled-in config.yaml showing all fields: schema, context, rules, operations. Demonstrates the expected structure and content.

```yaml
schema: spec-driven

context: |
  Tech stack: TypeScript, React, Node.js
  We use conventional commits
  Domain: e-commerce platform

rules:
  proposal:
    - Keep proposals under 500 words
    - Always include a "Non-goals" section
  tasks:
    - Break tasks into chunks of max 2 hours

operations:
  apply:
    guidance:
      - Keep test summaries concise
  archive:
    guidance:
      - Summarize the archive outcome before finishing

```

### Project Configuration > Artifact IDs by Schema

Source: https://github.com/fission-ai/openspec/blob/main/docs/opsx.md

**spec-driven** (default):
- `proposal` — Change proposal
- `specs` — Specifications
- `design` — Technical design
- `tasks` — Implementation tasks

/**
 * Claude Code Command Adapter
 *
 * Formats commands for Claude Code following its frontmatter specification.
 */
import path from 'path';
import { escapeYamlValue, formatTagsArray } from '../yaml.js';
import { OPENSPEC_CLI_ALLOWED_TOOLS } from '../../shared/allowed-tools.js';
/**
 * Claude Code adapter for command generation.
 * File path: .claude/commands/opsx/<id>.md
 * Frontmatter: name, description, allowed-tools, category, tags
 */
export const claudeAdapter = {
    toolId: 'claude',
    getFilePath(commandId) {
        return path.join('.claude', 'commands', 'opsx', `${commandId}.md`);
    },
    formatFile(content) {
        return `---
name: ${escapeYamlValue(content.name)}
description: ${escapeYamlValue(content.description)}
allowed-tools: ${OPENSPEC_CLI_ALLOWED_TOOLS}
category: ${escapeYamlValue(content.category)}
tags: ${formatTagsArray(content.tags)}
---

${content.body}
`;
    },
};

/**
 * Command Generation Types
 *
 * Tool-agnostic interfaces for command generation.
 * These types separate "what to generate" from "how to format it".
 */
/**
 * Tool-agnostic command data.
 * Represents the content of a command without any tool-specific formatting.
 */
export interface CommandContent {
    /** Command identifier (e.g., 'explore', 'apply', 'new') */
    id: string;
    /** Human-readable name (e.g., 'OpenSpec Explore') */
    name: string;
    /** Brief description of command purpose */
    description: string;
    /** Grouping category (e.g., 'Workflow') */
    category: string;
    /** Array of tag strings */
    tags: string[];
    /** The command instruction content (body text) */
    body: string;
}
/**
 * Per-tool formatting strategy.
 * Each AI tool implements this interface to handle its specific file path
 * and frontmatter format requirements.
 */
export interface ToolCommandAdapter {
    /** Tool identifier matching AIToolOption.value (e.g., 'claude', 'cursor') */
    toolId: string;
    /**
     * Returns the file path for a command.
     * @param commandId - The command identifier (e.g., 'explore')
     * @returns Path from project root (e.g., '.claude/commands/opsx/explore.md').
     *          May be absolute for tools with global-scoped command files.
     */
    getFilePath(commandId: string): string;
    /**
     * What the user types before the command name, when it is not the default
     * `/`. Amazon Q loads these files into its prompt library, which is invoked
     * with `@` (`@opsx-propose`), so its adapter sets '@'. The name itself is
     * still derived from getFilePath — see invocation.ts.
     */
    invocationPrefix?: string;
    /**
     * Formats the complete file content including frontmatter.
     * @param content - The tool-agnostic command content
     * @returns Complete file content ready to write
     */
    formatFile(content: CommandContent): string;
}
/**
 * Result of generating a command file.
 */
export interface GeneratedCommand {
    /** File path from project root, or absolute for global-scoped command files */
    path: string;
    /** Complete file content (frontmatter + body) */
    fileContent: string;
}

# OpenSpec Commands Reference

OpenSpec provides slash commands for AI coding assistants organized into two workflow profiles:

## Core Profile (Default)
The streamlined path includes six commands:

- **`/opsx:propose`** - "Create a new change and generate planning artifacts in one step"
- **`/opsx:explore`** - Investigates codebase and clarifies requirements before committing code
- **`/opsx:apply`** - Implements tasks from the change, working through a task list
- **`/opsx:update`** - Revises planning artifacts while maintaining coherence across them
- **`/opsx:sync`** - Merges delta specs into main specifications
- **`/opsx:archive`** - Finalizes and moves completed changes to archive folder

## Expanded Workflow Commands
Additional commands available when custom workflows are enabled:

- **`/opsx:new`** - Scaffolds a new change folder without generating artifacts
- **`/opsx:continue`** - Creates one artifact at a time following dependency chains
- **`/opsx:ff`** - "Fast-forward through artifact creation" for all planning artifacts simultaneously
- **`/opsx:verify`** - Validates implementation against artifacts across completeness, correctness, and coherence dimensions
- **`/opsx:bulk-archive`** - Archives multiple changes while resolving spec conflicts
- **`/opsx:onboard`** - Interactive guided tutorial through the complete workflow cycle

## Tool-Specific Syntax
Command registration varies across integrations:

| Integration Type | Format | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Command files | `/opsx:command` | Claude Code, Gemini CLI |
| Workflow files | `/opsx-command` | Cursor, Devin Desktop, GitHub Copilot IDE |
| Skills only | `/openspec-command` | CodeArts, ForgeCode, Zed Agent |

## Legacy Commands
Older all-at-once workflow commands remain functional but OPSX commands are recommended: `/openspec:proposal`, `/openspec:apply`, and `/openspec:archive`.

# OpenSpec CLI Reference Summary

The OpenSpec CLI provides comprehensive commands across multiple categories for managing specification-driven development workflows.

## Core Command Categories

**Setup & Configuration:** `init` and `update` handle project initialization and CLI upgrades. The `init` command supports interactive or non-interactive modes with options like `--tools`, `--language`, and `--profile`.

**Store Management:** Commands like `store setup`, `store register`, `store list`, and `store doctor` manage standalone OpenSpec repositories. These enable "working with multiple OpenSpec roots through a unified registry system."

**Browsing & Inspection:** `list`, `show`, and `view` provide navigation capabilities. The `view` command launches "an interactive dashboard for exploring specs and changes," while `list` and `show` support JSON output for programmatic access.

**Validation & Lifecycle:** `validate` checks structural integrity and spec deltas, supporting `--all`, `--strict`, and `--archived` flags. The `archive` command "moves the change folder to `openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/`" after merging delta specs.

**Workflow Support:** `new change`, `status`, `instructions`, `templates`, and `schemas` guide artifact-driven development. These support both human-readable and JSON outputs for agent integration.

**Schema Management:** `schema init`, `schema fork`, `schema validate`, and `schema which` enable custom workflow creation and debugging.

**Configuration:** `openspec config` manages global settings, including telemetry control via `OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY=0` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1`.

## Key Behavioral Notes

Archive validation can be skipped with `--no-validate`, though this disables capability retirement. The `--archived` flag specifically "verifies that every change under `changes/archive/` has all of its `tasks.md` checkboxes ticked."

Worksets provide "personal, named view[s] of the folders you work on together," stored locally and never committed. Context references are read-only and never override where commands execute.

Schema precedence follows this order: project → user → package defaults.

# OpenSpec Workflows Summary

OpenSpec fundamentally differs from traditional phase-locked approaches. Rather than forcing work through sequential stages, it treats commands as flexible actions you can repeat and revisit.

## Core Philosophy

The system embraces what the documentation calls **"Actions, not phases."** As stated: *"Commands are things you can do, not stages you're stuck in."* This means exploration and verification remain optional, and you can update planning documents whenever implementation reveals new information.

## Default Quick Path (`core` profile)

New installations use the `core` profile with six primary commands:

- `/opsx:explore` — optional investigation before committing
- `/opsx:propose` — create a change with initial planning artifacts
- `/opsx:apply` — implement tasks from your plan
- `/opsx:update` — refine planning documents mid-work
- `/opsx:sync` — merge specification changes into main specs
- `/opsx:archive` — finalize and move change to archive

The typical sequence: explore (if needed) → propose → apply → sync → archive.

## Expanded Workflow (Custom Selection)

Users can enable additional scaffold-and-control commands via `openspec config profile`:

- `/opsx:new` — explicitly start a change
- `/opsx:continue` — create the next artifact step-by-step
- `/opsx:ff` — generate all planning artifacts at once
- `/opsx:verify` — validate implementation against artifacts
- `/opsx:bulk-archive` — archive multiple completed changes together
- `/opsx:onboard` — team onboarding

## Key Decision Points

**Use `/opsx:ff` when:** You have clear requirements and need to move quickly.

**Use `/opsx:continue` when:** You're exploring as you go and want to review each step.

**Update existing changes when:** The intent stays the same but execution refines. Start fresh when scope fundamentally shifts or the original work can stand alone.

## Verification & Completion

Before archiving, `/opsx:verify` checks three dimensions:

- **Completeness:** All tasks marked done, requirements implemented, scenarios tested
- **Correctness:** Implementation matches spec intent and handles edge cases
- **Coherence:** Design decisions reflected in code structure and naming

`/opsx:archive` then prompts to sync unmerged specifications before moving the change to the archive folder.

/**
 * Profile System
 *
 * Defines workflow profiles that control which workflows are installed.
 * Profiles determine WHICH workflows; delivery (in global config) determines HOW.
 */
/**
 * Core workflows included in the 'core' profile.
 * These provide the streamlined experience for new users.
 */
export const CORE_WORKFLOWS = ['propose', 'explore', 'apply', 'update', 'sync', 'archive'];
/**
 * All available workflows in the system.
 */
export const ALL_WORKFLOWS = [
    'propose',
    'explore',
    'new',
    'continue',
    'apply',
    'update',
    'ff',
    'sync',
    'archive',
    'bulk-archive',
    'verify',
    'onboard',
];
/**
 * Resolves which workflows should be active for a given profile configuration.
 *
 * - 'core' profile always returns CORE_WORKFLOWS
 * - 'custom' profile returns the provided customWorkflows and required dependencies
 */
export function getProfileWorkflows(profile, customWorkflows) {
    if (profile === 'custom') {
        const workflows = customWorkflows ?? [];
        const syncDependentIndex = workflows.findIndex((workflow) => workflow === 'archive' || workflow === 'bulk-archive');
        if (syncDependentIndex !== -1 && !workflows.includes('sync')) {
            return [
                ...workflows.slice(0, syncDependentIndex),
                'sync',
                ...workflows.slice(syncDependentIndex),
            ];
        }
        return workflows;
    }
    return CORE_WORKFLOWS;
}

---
name: "OPSX: Propose"
description: "Propose a new change - create it and generate all artifacts in one step"
allowed-tools: Bash(openspec:*)
category: "Workflow"
tags: ["workflow", "artifacts", "experimental"]
---

Propose a new change - create the change and generate all artifacts in one step.

**Planning boundary**: This workflow creates planning artifacts only. The user request that selected or triggered this workflow authorizes planning only, even if it asks to build or fix something. Do not edit project code. After the planning artifacts are complete, stop. Do not start implementation in the same response, even if the initial request asks for it. Wait for a new user request after the artifacts are presented; then start the apply workflow.

I'll create a change with the artifacts your schema defines. With the default spec-driven schema that is:
- proposal.md (what & why)
- `specs/<capability-path>/spec.md` (what the system must do - a delta, not the main spec)
- design.md (how)
- tasks.md (implementation steps)

`<capability-path>` is the spec directory relative to `specs/` (for example, `user-auth` or `identity/user-auth`). Preserve an existing capability's full path and follow the project's established organization for new capabilities.

When the user is ready to implement, they must start the apply workflow explicitly.

---

**Store selection:** If the user names a store (a store is a standalone OpenSpec repo registered on this machine) or the work lives in one, run `openspec store list --json` to discover registered store ids, then pass `--store <id>` on the commands that read or write specs and changes (`new change`, `status`, `instructions`, `list`, `show`, `validate`, `archive`, `doctor`, `context`, `schemas`, `view`). Once selected, treat `--store <id>` as sticky for the rest of the workflow. Every unscoped example of those commands below is shorthand: before running it, append the flag. For example, run `openspec status --change "<name>" --json --store "<id>"`, not the unscoped form shown below. Other commands do not take the flag. Hints printed by commands already carry the flag; keep it on follow-ups. Without a store, commands act on the nearest local `openspec/` root.

**Project check:** These steps expect a project that already uses OpenSpec. Before the first step that writes anything (`new change`, `archive`, `sync specs`, or authoring an artifact file), confirm the project has a root: run `openspec list --json` (with `--store <id>` when a store is selected, since the store is then the root) and read `root`. A root object means the project is set up. `"root": null` means it is not - there is no `openspec/` directory here, and a write such as `openspec new change` would create one as a side effect. The command also exits non-zero, which is that answer rather than a broken CLI, so read the JSON instead of retrying or working around it.

One `"root": null` is not about setup: when a `status` error message starts with `Declared in` or `Invalid store declaration in` and names this project's `openspec/config.yaml` (or `config.yml`), the project does use OpenSpec through a store it declares, which this machine cannot resolve (the store is not registered, or the `store:` line is malformed). Do not treat it as uninitialized and skip the branches below: stop before writing and show the user that error's `message` and `fix`.

Otherwise, with no root, what happens next depends on how this workflow was reached:

- **Auto-selected**: you chose this workflow yourself, without the user naming OpenSpec, naming this skill, or running its slash command. Stop using OpenSpec and answer the request normally, as you would with no OpenSpec installed. Do not ask them to set anything up and do not mention OpenSpec setup.
- **Explicit OpenSpec request**: the user named OpenSpec, named this skill, or ran its slash command. Stop before writing and ask how to proceed: set this project up (`openspec init`), target a store they already have (`--store <id>`), or continue without OpenSpec for this request. Wait for their answer.

In both branches, never create the root as a side effect: do not run `openspec init` until the user asks for it, do not hand-create `openspec/` files, and do not let a command create it.

**Input**: The argument after `/opsx:propose` is the change name (kebab-case), OR a description of what the user wants to build.

**Steps**

1. **Understand the request and clarify material ambiguity**

   If no input is provided, ask the user (open-ended, no preset options):
   > "What change do you want to work on? Describe what you want to build or fix."

   From their description, derive a kebab-case name (e.g., "add user authentication" → `add-user-auth`).

   **IMPORTANT**: Do NOT proceed without understanding what the user wants to build.

   If the request contains ambiguity that would materially affect scope, externally observable behavior, compatibility, or acceptance criteria, ask the user before creating the change. For minor details, make a reasonable assumption and record it in the planning artifacts.

2. **Load project context**

   Run `openspec context --json` from the current working directory (or `openspec context --json --store "<store-id>"` when a registered store was explicitly selected). Use the returned `root.path` as the authoritative OpenSpec root. If context reports `no_openspec_root`, stop without creating or changing any files and follow the **Project check** above for how this workflow was reached. Offer `openspec init` only for an explicit OpenSpec request, and wait for the user to request initialization. Do not initialize automatically or run `openspec new change`. After initialization, rerun this context check before continuing. For any other context failure, stop and report the error; do not fall back to the current directory or run later OpenSpec commands without the selected store.

   Only when context returns a resolved `root.path`, read `<root.path>/openspec/config.yaml`. Use `config.yml` only when `config.yaml` does not exist. If neither file exists, continue without project context. Do not fall back to `config.yml` if `config.yaml` is unreadable or invalid.

   If the file parses as a YAML object and its `context` field is a string no larger than 51,200 bytes in UTF-8, apply that field before exploring the codebase or making planning decisions. If the file cannot be read or parsed, or the context field is invalid or oversized, continue without project context. Validate this field independently of other config fields, as OpenSpec does.

# OpenSpec Getting Started Summary

OpenSpec is a workflow tool that helps you and an AI assistant agree on what to build before writing code.

## Setup (Terminal Only)

```
$ npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec@latest
$ cd your-project && openspec init
```

Then you work entirely in your AI chat with slash commands.

## The Core Workflow

According to the guide, the basic flow involves five chat commands:

1. **`/opsx:explore`** (optional) — Think through your idea first
2. **`/opsx:propose <change-name>`** — AI drafts the plan
3. **`/opsx:apply`** — AI builds the implementation
4. **`/opsx:sync`** — Update specs
5. **`/opsx:archive`** — File away the completed change

## What Gets Created

Running `/opsx:propose add-dark-mode` generates:
- `proposal.md` — The "why" and scope
- `specs/` folder — Delta specs showing what's changing
- `design.md` — Technical approach
- `tasks.md` — Implementation checklist

## Verification Commands

After changes are made, use the CLI to review:

```bash
openspec list      # Active changes
openspec show <name>
openspec validate <name>
openspec view      # Interactive dashboard
```

The key principle: **"Delta specs are the key concept in OpenSpec. They show what's changing"** relative to your current system specifications.

# OpenSpec Changelog: Versions 1.14.0 and 1.13.x

## Version 1.14.0

**Minor Changes:**

- Code Studio integrated as an `init` and `update` target with project skills and `.prompt.md` commands under `.codestudio/`
- DeepSeek Harness support via `openspec init --tools dsh`, installing skills to `.dsh/skills/`
- GigaCode added as supported `--tools` target with skills in `.gigacode/skills/openspec-*/SKILL.md`
- AtomCode support through `openspec init --tools atomcode` with skills in `.atomcode/skills/` and `/opsx-<id>` commands
- GSD support: "Install OpenSpec workflows as project skills with `openspec init --tools gsd`"
- Amp support: "select `amp` during init to install OpenSpec workflows as project skills under `.agents/skills/`"
- Version reports with `openspec version` command including `--check` and `--json` flags
- EasyCode support for init and update with project-local skills and TOML commands
- Nix overlay exposure through `overlays.default`
- Grok Build added as skills-only tool via `openspec init --tools grok`
- Warp support through project-local skills in `.warp/skills`
- Dashboard workflow status in `openspec view` showing artifact progress states
- `openspec-archive-change` skill no longer calls uninstalled skills; merges delta specs itself

**Patch Changes:**

- IBM Bob product name displayed correctly in tool picker and success messages
- AI-assisted migration guidance from legacy `project.md` to `config.yaml`
- Proposal authors guided toward durable, behavior-based capability names
- Apply edits target correct task with `sourcePath` and `line` in JSON output
- Archive stops on failed spec sync with blocking conditions
- Store-only repositories can run `openspec init` at repo root
- Legacy cleanup files deletion warnings with backup recommendations
- Config guidance keeps project documentation and codebase facts out of `config.yaml`
- Specs instruction clarifies 500-character requirement length requirement
- `show --json` includes requirement and scenario `name` fields for citation
- Store-backed changes: `status --json` fixed for `actionContext.allowedEditRoots`
- Rule list validation errors now name offending index and YAML shape
- Change metadata validation warns on unrecognized `.openspec.yaml` keys
- Shell completion uninstall preserves file state exactly as install found it

## Version 1.13.2

**Patch Changes:**

- Archive workflow uses schema-aware task progress from `openspec list --json`
- Artifact output resolution recognizes brace expansion and extglob patterns
- Continue commands instruct to follow active OpenSpec workflow directly
- Kilo Code commands generated in `.kilo/command/` instead of `.kilocode/workflows/`

- Scenario-loss guard messaging explains which scenarios each side introduces

- Task guidance requires each task group to land its own tests and documentation
- `openspec update --force` returns nonzero when unable to replace legacy-only Codex
- `/opsx:update` can fill missing files under satisfied glob artifacts
- `/opsx:verify` correctly handles REMOVED requirements and skipped checks
- Archive lock file handling fixed on Windows device ID reporting
- Bash completion uninstall preserves `.bashrc` exactly as install found it

- Bulk archive prevents nesting change inside existing archive target
- Config editor now accepts programs with arguments (e.g., `code --wait`)

**Non-Goals:**
- Live scraping on every request.

# Proposal

## Why

Users need to collect products into a basket and manage quantities before checkout; without it the catalog is read-only and not useful for purchases.

## What Changes

- Add a `basket` capability: add, update quantity, remove items.
- Modify `product-catalog` so each product exposes a stable id usable by the basket.

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `basket`: Per-user basket with add, update and delete operations.

### Modified Capabilities
- `product-catalog`: products must carry a stable `id`.

## Impact

- New `/api/basket` routes; catalog payload gains `id`.
EOF
cat > "$C/specs/basket/spec.md" <<'EOF'
# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Lets a shopper collect catalog products into a basket and manage item quantities before purchase.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Shopper can add a product to the basket
The system SHALL add the selected product to the shopper's basket with quantity 1 when it is not already present.

#### Scenario: Add new product
- **WHEN** the shopper adds a product that is not in the basket
- **THEN** the basket contains that product with quantity 1

### Requirement: Shopper can update item quantity
The system SHALL update the quantity of a basket item to any positive integer.

#### Scenario: Update quantity
- **WHEN** the shopper sets quantity 3 on a basket item
- **THEN** the basket item quantity is 3

### Requirement: Shopper can remove an item
The system SHALL remove a basket item when the shopper deletes it.

#### Scenario: Remove item
- **WHEN** the shopper deletes a basket item
- **THEN** the item is no longer in the basket
EOF
cat > "$C/specs/product-catalog/spec.md" <<'EOF'
# Spec Delta

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Catalog lists aggregated products
The system SHALL return a list of products aggregated from all integrated shops, each with a stable id, name, price, image and source shop.

#### Scenario: Catalog is requested
- **WHEN** a client requests `GET /api/products`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array of products from every integrated shop

#### Scenario: Product ids are stable
- **WHEN** the catalog is requested twice
- **THEN** every product keeps the same id across both responses
EOF
cat > "$C/design.md" <<'EOF'
# Design

## Context

See proposal.md. Basket is per browser session.

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- Simple in-memory or local-storage basket.

**Non-Goals:**
- Checkout and payment.

## Decisions

- Basket state lives server-side keyed by session id; alternative localStorage rejected to keep one source of truth.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Session loss clears basket] → acceptable for MVP.
EOF
cat > "$C/tasks.md" <<'EOF'
# Tasks

## 1. Basket API

- [x] 1.1 Implement add/update/delete basket routes and verify with unit tests
- [x] 1.2 Add stable product ids to the catalog payload and verify contract test
EOF

- `product-catalog`: products must carry a stable `id`.

# product-catalog Specification

## Purpose
Provides a single read-only catalog that aggregates products from several integrated organic shops.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Catalog lists aggregated products
The system SHALL return a list of products aggregated from all integrated shops, each with a stable id, name, price, image and source shop.

#### Scenario: Catalog is requested
- **WHEN** a client requests `GET /api/products`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array of products from every integrated shop

#### Scenario: Product ids are stable
- **WHEN** the catalog is requested twice
- **THEN** every product keeps the same id across both responses
=====basket spec=====
# basket Specification

## Purpose
Lets a shopper collect catalog products into a basket and manage item quantities before purchase.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Shopper can add a product to the basket
The system SHALL add the selected product to the shopper's basket with quantity 1 when it is not already present.

#### Scenario: Add new product
- **WHEN** the shopper adds a product that is not in the basket
- **THEN** the basket contains that product with quantity 1

### Requirement: Shopper can update item quantity
The system SHALL update the quantity of a basket item to any positive integer.

#### Scenario: Update quantity
- **WHEN** the shopper sets quantity 3 on a basket item
- **THEN** the basket item quantity is 3

### Requirement: Shopper can remove an item
The system SHALL remove a basket item when the shopper deletes it.

#### Scenario: Remove item
- **WHEN** the shopper deletes a basket item
- **THEN** the item is no longer in the basket

input.configYaml:
Keys accepted in openspec/config.yaml (from dist/core/project-config.js, 1.13.1):
- schema (string, REQUIRED): workflow schema name; built-in is "spec-driven" (only one shipped; list with `openspec schemas`). A project-local schema lives in openspec/schemas/<name>/ (create with `openspec schema init <name>` or `openspec schema fork spec-driven <name>`).
- context (string, optional, max 50 KB = 51,200 bytes UTF-8; larger is ignored with a warning): injected into EVERY artifact instruction (`openspec instructions ... --json` returns it as `context`). Put tech stack, conventions, domain facts, constraints - not docs or codebase listings.
- rules (map artifact-id -> list of strings, optional): appended only to that artifact's instruction. Artifact ids for spec-driven: proposal, specs, design, tasks.
- operations (optional): operations.apply.guidance / operations.archive.guidance -> list of strings (advisory, returned as `operationGuidance` by `openspec instructions apply|archive`). Only `guidance` is a supported sub-field.
- store (optional): id of a registered standalone store to use as the planning root (stores feature, beta) - leave out for a normal repo.
- githubCopilot.cloudAgent (bool, optional): written by init when you choose/decline Copilot cloud agent files.
- language (optional, written by `init --language`): language for new artifacts. (unconfirmed exact key name - not exercised locally)
Invalid fields are warned about and ignored (not fatal). config.yml is accepted only when config.yaml does not exist.

  Stack: TypeScript, pnpm workspace (apps/web, apps/api), Node 22.
  Testing: Vitest for unit/contract tests, Playwright for e2e; every task must be verified by a test or command.
  Conventions: conventional commits; kebab-case capability names (product-catalog, basket, shop-import).
  Practices to prove: SDD (OpenSpec), AGENTS.md context rules, loop engineering, maker != checker review pass.

rules:
  proposal:
    - Keep proposals under 500 words
    - Always include a "Non-goals" subsection under Impact
  specs:
    - Every requirement uses SHALL; every scenario uses WHEN/THEN bullets
    - Reference the external shop by name in scenarios that depend on it
  design:
    - Document which data is scraped vs seeded and how it is refreshed
  tasks:
    - Each task names the test or command that verifies it
    - Break tasks into chunks of max 2 hours

operations:
  apply:
    guidance:
      - Run the focused test for the task before the full suite
      - Mark a task [x] only after its verification passes
  archive:
    guidance:
      - Summarize which specs were merged before finishing

Per-change metadata file openspec/changes/<id>/.openspec.yaml (schema in dist/core/change-metadata/schema.js):
schema: spec-driven            # required
created: 2026-10-04            # YYYY-MM-DD, written by `new change`
goal: optional free text       # from `new change --goal`
affected_areas: [..]           # optional
skip_specs: true               # declares a zero-delta change (refactor/tooling/docs); validate accepts no deltas; MUST NOT coexist with files under specs/
retire_capabilities: true      # allows archive to delete a main spec whose last requirement is REMOVED
input.workflowCommands:
Claude Code invocation form is `/opsx:<workflow>` (namespaced command files .claude/commands/opsx/<workflow>.md); each also exists as an auto-triggerable skill .claude/skills/openspec-<name>/SKILL.md. All are generated by `openspec init --tools claude` / `openspec update`. Other tools use `/opsx-<workflow>` (Cursor, Copilot) or `/openspec-<workflow>` (skills-only tools) - irrelevant for Claude Code.

CORE profile (installed by default - 6 commands, verified):
- /opsx:propose <name-or-description>  (skill openspec-propose) - "Propose a new change - create it and generate all artifacts in one step". Runs `openspec context --json`, derives kebab-case name, `openspec new change "<name>"`, then for each artifact `openspec instructions <artifact> --change "<name>" --json` and writes proposal.md -> specs/<cap>/spec.md -> design.md -> tasks.md, re-checking `openspec status --change "<name>" --json`. PLANNING ONLY: it explicitly refuses to touch project code and stops after artifacts; you must then run /opsx:apply in a new message.
- /opsx:explore [topic]  (openspec-explore) - "Enter explore mode - think through ideas, investigate problems, clarify requirements". Read-only thinking partner; optional before propose.
- /opsx:apply [change-name]  (openspec-apply-change) - "Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change". This IS the "implement" step (there is no /opsx:implement). Runs `openspec status --change X --json` and `openspec instructions apply --change X --json`, works through tasks.md, flips `- [ ]` to `- [x]` immediately after each task passes its verification, pauses on blockers. Auto-selects the change if only one is active.
- /opsx:update [change-name]  (openspec-update-change) - "Update a change - revise existing planning artifacts and keep them coherent". Drafts edits to proposal/specs/design/tasks, applies after your confirmation, never edits code. (Not to be confused with CLI `openspec update`, which regenerates .claude/ files.)
- /opsx:sync [change-name]  (openspec-sync-specs) - "Sync delta specs from a change to main specs". AGENT-DRIVEN merge: the agent reads each delta and edits openspec/specs/<cap>/spec.md directly (can add one scenario without rewriting the requirement), creates missing main specs from ADDED, then runs `openspec validate --specs`. Use when you want main specs updated before/without archiving.
- /opsx:archive [change-name]  (openspec-archive-change) - "Archive a completed change". Checks `openspec status --change X --json` completeness and task progress, loads `openspec instructions archive --change X --json` (context + operationGuidance), offers to run the /opsx:sync workflow inline for unsynced deltas (in 1.13.1 it delegates to the sync skill; 1.14.0 merges itself), then moves the change dir to openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/ (same naming rule as the CLI). The pure-CLI equivalent that does a programmatic merge is `openspec archive <name> --yes`.

EXPANDED workflows (available in 1.13.1 but NOT installed until you set profile=custom + workflows list, see init; verified they then appear as /opsx:* files):
- /opsx:new <name>  (openspec-new-change) - "Start a new change using the experimental artifact workflow" - scaffolds the change dir only (= `openspec new change`), no artifacts.
- /opsx:continue [name]  (openspec-continue-change) - "Continue working on a change - create the next artifact" - one artifact per invocation following the dependency graph; review between steps.
- /opsx:ff [name]  (openspec-ff-change) - "Create a change and generate all artifacts needed for implementation in one go" - fast-forward; functionally close to propose but starts from an existing /opsx:new change or a name.
- /opsx:verify [name]  (openspec-verify-change) - "Verify implementation matches change artifacts before archiving" - checks completeness (tasks done, requirements implemented, scenarios tested), correctness, coherence; reports gaps. Good "checker" pass for maker != checker.
- /opsx:bulk-archive  (openspec-bulk-archive-change) - "Archive multiple completed changes at once", resolving cross-change spec conflicts.
- /opsx:onboard  (openspec-onboard) - "Guided onboarding - walk through a complete OpenSpec workflow cycle with narration".

Typical loop for this project: /opsx:explore (optional) -> /opsx:propose "<idea>" -> review openspec/changes/<id>/* + `openspec validate <id> --strict` -> /opsx:apply <id> -> (optional /opsx:verify <id> if enabled) -> /opsx:archive <id> (or `openspec archive <id> --yes`). The user asked for "propose, implement, archive": implement = /opsx:apply.

DEPRECATED / LEGACY (do not use; not generated by 1.13.1): `/openspec:proposal`, `/openspec:apply`, `/openspec:archive` (old all-at-once commands in .claude/commands/openspec/, plus the `<!-- OPENSPEC:START -->` block in root AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and openspec/AGENTS.md, openspec/project.md). `openspec init --force` / `openspec update` delete the OpenSpec-written legacy command files and strip the markers. Also deprecated CLI: `openspec change list` (use `openspec list`), `--requirements-only` (use `--deltas-only`). Tags in command frontmatter still say "experimental" for the OPSX workflow - that is the current, recommended path per the docs.

All syntax from `openspec <cmd> --help` on 1.13.1. Every root-reading command accepts `--store <id>` (ignore unless using stores) and most accept `--json`.

Setup
  openspec init [path] [--tools claude|all|none|<list>] [--language <lang>] [--force] [--profile core|custom] [--no-animation] [--copilot-cloud|--no-copilot-cloud]
  openspec update [path] [--force]                    # regenerate .claude/ skills+commands after CLI upgrade / profile change
  openspec config path | list | get <key> | set [--string] [--allow-unknown] <key> <value> | unset <key> | reset | edit | profile [core]
      # global keys: profile (core|custom), delivery (both|skills|commands), workflows (JSON array), defaultStore, telemetry.enabled, featureFlags.<flag>
  openspec completion generate|install|uninstall [bash|zsh|fish|powershell]
  openspec feedback <message> [--body <text>]

Changes
  openspec new change <name> [--description <text>] [--goal <text>] [--schema <name>] [--json]   # creates openspec/changes/<name>/.openspec.yaml (+README.md if --description); name must be kebab-case
  openspec status [--change <id>] [--all] [--schema <name>] [--json]        # artifact completion ([x]/[ ]/[-] blocked) + "Next:" command
  openspec instructions <proposal|specs|design|tasks|apply|archive> --change <id> [--schema <name>] [--json]   # enriched instruction + template + context + rules + resolvedOutputPath
  openspec templates [--schema spec-driven] [--json]
  openspec schemas [--json]
  openspec schema which|validate [name] | fork <source> [name] | init <name>   # experimental custom workflows
  openspec list [--specs | --changes] [--sort recent|name] [--json]          # changes show "n/m tasks"; `openspec list --specs` = capability inventory
  openspec show <item> [--type change|spec] [--json] [--deltas-only] [--diff] [--requirements] [--no-scenarios] [-r <n>] [--no-interactive]
      # `openspec show <change> --diff` prints proposal + per-requirement diff vs main specs; `--json --deltas-only` shows parsed deltas (debug "no deltas" errors)
  openspec change show|validate <name> [...]           # older aliases; `openspec change list` is DEPRECATED
  openspec spec show|list|validate [spec-id] [...]
  openspec view                                        # interactive TUI dashboard
  openspec doctor [--json] ; openspec context [--json] [--code-workspace <path> --force]

Validation
  openspec validate [item-name] [--type change|spec] [--strict] [--json] [--no-interactive]
  openspec validate --all [--strict] [--report full|findings] [--concurrency <n>]   # CI: `openspec validate --all --strict` -> exit 0 only if every change AND spec passes (verified)
  openspec validate --changes | --specs
  openspec validate --archived                         # fails if any archived change has an unchecked task (pre-commit lint)
  Output example: "✓ change/add-product-catalog\nTotals: 1 passed, 0 failed (1 items)"; single item: "Change 'x' is valid" / "Change 'x' has issues\n✗ [ERROR] file: ..."

Archive
  openspec archive <change-name> [-y|--yes] [--skip-specs] [--no-validate] [--json]
    - validates the change first (delta rules + merge dry-run); on failure: "Validation failed for change 'x'. Run openspec validate x ..." (exit non-zero) - `--no-validate` requires confirmation/--yes.
    - incomplete tasks: interactive prompt, or with --json an error {code: "archive_tasks_incomplete", fix: "Complete the tasks or rerun with --yes."}; `--yes` continues with a warning.
    - merges deltas into openspec/specs/<cap>/spec.md (prints "Specs to update: product-catalog: create" / "+ 1 added ~ 0 - 0 → 0" / "Specs updated successfully."), creating the main spec for new capabilities (title "# <cap> Specification", Purpose copied from the delta's ## Purpose, else placeholder "TBD - created by archiving change <name>. Update Purpose after archive.").
    - then moves openspec/changes/<name>/ -> openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/ (local date; a name already prefixed is not re-prefixed). Prints "Change 'x' archived as '2026-10-04-x'."
    - `--skip-specs` archives without touching main specs (tooling/doc-only changes); `--json` gives {archive:{change, archivedAs, path, specsUpdated, totals:{added,modified,removed,renamed}}}.
    - Change names starting with "-" need `openspec archive --yes -- <name>`.

Non-interactive/CI tip: pass `--no-interactive` (validate/show) and `--json`; concurrency env OPENSPEC_CONCURRENCY. Telemetry: OPENSPEC_TELEMETRY=0.

Verified end-to-end sequence (1.13.1):
  openspec new change add-product-catalog --description "..."   # -> .openspec.yaml, README.md
  # write proposal.md, specs/product-catalog/spec.md, design.md, tasks.md
  openspec validate --all --strict --no-interactive              # ✓ change/add-product-catalog
  openspec status --change add-product-catalog                   # 4/4 artifacts complete, Next: openspec instructions apply ...
  # implement, tick tasks - [x]
  openspec archive add-product-catalog --yes                     # merges, moves to archive/2026-10-04-add-product-catalog
  openspec validate --all --strict ; openspec validate --archived
input.specFormat:
Parser facts (dist/core/parsers + validation, 1.13.1): headings are matched case-insensitively; section headers are `##`, requirements `### Requirement: <name>`, scenarios MUST be `#### Scenario: <name>` (exactly 4 hashes - 3 hashes or bullet-only scenarios "fail silently" / are not counted); scenario bodies are bullet lines `- **WHEN** ...` / `- **THEN** ...` (and `- **AND** ...`, `- **GIVEN**` accepted as free text); requirement body SHOULD contain the English keyword SHALL or MUST (missing keyword = WARNING, which FAILS under --strict); every ADDED/MODIFIED requirement needs >= 1 scenario (ERROR); requirement text > 500 chars = INFO; delta spec must live at specs/<capability-path>/spec.md (a file at specs/spec.md is an ERROR and ignored by archive); capability path segments kebab-case.

A) MAIN spec (openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md) - what archive produces/maintains; passes `openspec validate --all --strict` (verified):

# product-catalog Specification

## Purpose
Provides a single read-only catalog that aggregates products from several integrated organic shops.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Catalog lists aggregated products
The system SHALL return a list of products aggregated from all integrated shops, each with name, price, image and source shop.

#### Scenario: Catalog is requested
- **WHEN** a client requests `GET /api/products`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array of products from every integrated shop

Rules: required headers "## Purpose" and "## Requirements"; Purpose >= 50 chars (shorter = WARNING = strict fail), not a TBD/TODO placeholder; at least one requirement; main specs must NEVER contain ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED headers.

B) DELTA spec (openspec/changes/<id>/specs/<capability-path>/spec.md) - minimal NEW-capability delta that passed `openspec validate <id> --strict` and archived cleanly (verified):

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Provides a single read-only catalog that aggregates products from several integrated organic shops.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Catalog lists aggregated products
The system SHALL return a list of products aggregated from all integrated shops, each with name, price, image and source shop.

#### Scenario: Catalog is requested
- **WHEN** a client requests `GET /api/products`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array of products from every integrated shop

C) Delta for an EXISTING capability (no ## Purpose - it is ignored for existing specs) using MODIFIED (verified; archive replaced the requirement block and kept both scenarios):

# Spec Delta

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Catalog lists aggregated products
The system SHALL return a list of products aggregated from all integrated shops, each with a stable id, name, price, image and source shop.

#### Scenario: Catalog is requested
- **WHEN** a client requests `GET /api/products`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array of products from every integrated shop

#### Scenario: Product ids are stable
- **WHEN** the catalog is requested twice
- **THEN** every product keeps the same id across both responses

D) All delta section forms (full template from the shipped sync skill):

## ADDED Requirements          # new requirements; appended to main spec
## MODIFIED Requirements       # header must match an existing `### Requirement:` name (whitespace-insensitive); MUST carry the FULL block (text + every surviving scenario) - a MODIFIED that drops a scenario the main spec has is rejected by validate and archive ("scenario-loss guard"); the whole block is replaced
## REMOVED Requirements        # only the header is needed to delete: `### Requirement: Deprecated Feature`; schema instruction says also add `**Reason**: ...` and `**Migration**: ...` lines (good practice; validator only parses names - enforcement unconfirmed)
## RENAMED Requirements        # bullet pairs: `- FROM: `### Requirement: Old Name`` then `- TO: `### Requirement: New Name``; must be complete pairs

Delta validation rules (validate / --strict): >= 1 delta across the change unless .openspec.yaml has skip_specs: true; no duplicate requirement names within a section; no cross-section conflicts (same name in ADDED+REMOVED, MODIFIED+ADDED, MODIFIED+REMOVED, RENAMED+REMOVED, RENAMED TO vs ADDED); MODIFIED must use the new name after a RENAME; delta description (first requirement sentence) >= 10 chars (WARNING); ADDED/MODIFIED section with zero parsed requirements (WARNING); > 10 deltas per change ("Consider splitting", level unconfirmed); requirements written outside any delta section are warned with line numbers and ignored. `--strict` = valid only when errors == 0 AND warnings == 0 (dist/core/validation/validator.js createReport). Archive merge semantics: ADDED -> appended under ## Requirements; MODIFIED -> block replaced by name; REMOVED -> block deleted (if it empties the spec, archive aborts unless retire_capabilities: true, which then deletes the main spec); RENAMED -> header renamed; new capability -> file created with "# <cap> Specification" + Purpose from delta + "## Requirements".
input.proposalTemplate:
Shipped templates (openspec templates --schema spec-driven). Validation that actually runs on them: proposal.md needs "## Why" (>= 50 chars; > 1000 chars warns) and "## What Changes" (non-empty); `openspec status` marks an artifact complete as soon as its file exists; tasks.md is parsed for checkboxes; design.md is not structurally validated (only existence). Use these exact headers:

--- proposal.md ---
# Proposal

## Why

<1-2 sentences, >= 50 characters: problem/opportunity and why now>

## What Changes

- <bullet per change; mark breaking ones **BREAKING**>

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities
- `<capability-path>`: <what this capability covers>     # each becomes specs/<capability-path>/spec.md (kebab-case)

### Modified Capabilities
- `<existing-capability-path>`: <which requirement changes>   # leave empty if none; must match a path under openspec/specs/

## Impact

- <affected code, APIs, dependencies, systems>

--- design.md ---
# Design

## Context

<current state and constraints; reference proposal.md, do not restate>

## Goals / Non-Goals

**Goals:**
- ...

**Non-Goals:**
- ...

## Decisions

- <decision>: <rationale>; alternatives considered: <...>

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Risk] → Mitigation

(optional) ## Migration Plan
(optional) ## Open Questions

--- tasks.md ---  (checkbox format is parsed by apply/list/archive/validate --archived)
# Tasks

## 1. <Task Group Name>

- [ ] 1.1 <task description that states how it is verified: test / command / observable behavior>
- [ ] 1.2 <...>

## 2. <Task Group Name>

- [ ] 2.1 <...>

Checkbox rules (schema.yaml instruction, verified counts in `openspec list` "0/3 tasks"): `- [ ]` = pending; `- [x]` / `- [X]` / `- [ x]` = done; `- [~]`, `- [-]`, `- []` = NOT done; a line without a checkbox is not tracked (a tasks.md with zero checkboxes triggers "This change counts as 0 tasks" warning); number tasks X.Y under `## N.` headings (ambiguous numbering is warned). /opsx:apply flips `- [ ]` -> `- [x]` right after each task's verification passes; `openspec archive` refuses incomplete tasks unless --yes; `openspec validate --archived` later fails on any unchecked box in archive/.
pitfalls: Version skew: global `openspec` is 1.13.1 but `pnpm add -D @fission-ai/openspec@latest` installs 1.14.0; `pnpm exec openspec` then uses 1.14.0 while generated .claude files were stamped generatedBy 1.13.1. Pin `@fission-ai/openspec@1.13.1` or regenerate with `pnpm exec openspec update --force` and keep one version.

Scenarios MUST use exactly `#### Scenario:` (4 hashes) with `- **WHEN**` / `- **THEN**` bullets; `### Scenario:` or plain bullets are silently not counted and the requirement then fails with 'Requirement must have at least one scenario'.
Delta specs must be at openspec/changes/<id>/specs/<capability-path>/spec.md. A file at specs/spec.md (no capability folder) is an ERROR and is ignored by apply/archive.

An empty/zero-delta change fails `openspec validate` ('Change must have at least one delta') unless .openspec.yaml has `skip_specs: true`; and skip_specs together with any file under specs/ is a conflict error.

`--strict` turns every WARNING into a failure: Purpose < 50 chars or a TBD/TODO placeholder, requirement body without SHALL/MUST, delta description < 10 chars, ADDED/MODIFIED section with no parsed requirement, tasks file without checkboxes. Run `openspec validate --all --strict --no-interactive` in CI and before every archive.

`## Purpose` in a delta is only read when the capability is NEW; for an existing capability it is ignored - edit openspec/specs/<cap>/spec.md directly to change Purpose. If a new-capability delta has no Purpose, archive writes the placeholder 'TBD - created by archiving change <name>. Update Purpose after archive.' which then fails --strict as a placeholder.

MODIFIED must contain the ENTIRE requirement block (text + all existing scenarios + new ones). Archive replaces the whole block by header name; a MODIFIED that omits a scenario present in the main spec is rejected ('scenario-loss guard'). Header text must match the main spec exactly (whitespace-insensitive). If you only add new concerns, use ADDED instead.
`/opsx:propose` is planning-only - it will not write code even if asked; implementation is `/opsx:apply <change>` in a NEW message. There is no /opsx:implement.

`openspec archive` with unticked tasks: interactive prompt, or error archive_tasks_incomplete under --json; use `--yes` to proceed (prints a warning). It also runs validation first; `--no-validate` needs `--yes` and is discouraged. `--skip-specs` means main specs are NOT updated.

In 1.13.1 the /opsx:archive skill performs an agent-driven merge via the /opsx:sync workflow (agent edits main specs by hand) rather than calling `openspec archive`; results can differ from the CLI's programmatic merge. For deterministic proof, run `openspec archive <id> --yes` and `openspec validate --all --strict` afterwards.

`openspec init --tools claude` in 1.13.1 does NOT create or touch AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md (that was the legacy layout). Write your own AGENTS.md for the context-engineering practice and keep OpenSpec's context in openspec/config.yaml `context:` (<= 50 KB). openspec/project.md is legacy - do not create it.

The expanded commands (/opsx:new, continue, ff, verify, bulk-archive, onboard) are NOT installed by default. Enable with `openspec config set profile custom` + `openspec config set workflows '[...]'` (global ~/.config/openspec/config.json) and rerun init/update. `openspec init --profile custom` without a workflows list installs ZERO skills/commands.

Generated command/skill files declare `allowed-tools: Bash(openspec:*)` and call the bare `openspec` binary, so it must be on PATH inside Claude Code (global install or node_modules/.bin on PATH). Restart/reload Claude Code after init so /opsx:* commands appear.

Change ids must be kebab-case (lowercase letters, digits, single hyphens). Never nest a change dir inside another (reported as 'namespace folder' and refused by archive). Archive prefixes the local date YYYY-MM-DD-; do not pre-prefix names.

`openspec list` (no flags) lists in-flight CHANGES, not specs; use `openspec list --specs` to see existing capabilities before naming a new one, and reuse exact existing paths for Modified Capabilities.

`openspec update` (CLI) regenerates .claude files and is different from `/opsx:update` (revises a change's planning artifacts). `openspec change list` and `--requirements-only` are deprecated aliases.

config.yaml `context` over 51,200 bytes is ignored with a warning; `rules` must be a map of artifact-id -> list of strings (ids: proposal, specs, design, tasks); unknown `operations.<op>` fields other than `guidance` are warned and ignored.

Trust the local dry run above.

Keys accepted in openspec/config.yaml (from dist/core/project-config.js, 1.13.1):
- schema (string, REQUIRED): workflow schema name; built-in is "spec-driven" (only one shipped; list with `openspec schemas`). A project-local schema lives in openspec/schemas/<name>/ (create with `openspec schema init <name>` or `openspec schema fork spec-driven <name>`).
- context (string, optional, max 50 KB = 51,200 bytes UTF-8; larger is ignored with a warning): injected into EVERY artifact instruction (`openspec instructions ... --json` returns it as `context`). Put tech stack, conventions, domain facts, constraints - not docs or codebase listings.
- rules (map artifact-id -> list of strings, optional): appended only to that artifact's instruction. Artifact ids for spec-driven: proposal, specs, design, tasks.
- operations (optional): operations.apply.guidance / operations.archive.guidance -> list of strings (advisory, returned as `operationGuidance` by `openspec instructions apply|archive`). Only `guidance` is a supported sub-field.
- store (optional): id of a registered standalone store to use as the planning root (stores feature, beta) - leave out for a normal repo.
- githubCopilot.cloudAgent (bool, optional): written by init when you choose/decline Copilot cloud agent files.
- language (optional, written by `init --language`): language for new artifacts. (unconfirmed exact key name - not exercised locally)
Invalid fields are warned about and ignored (not fatal). config.yml is accepted only when config.yaml does not exist.

Full example for this project (copy-paste into openspec/config.yaml):

schema: spec-driven

context: |
  Project: "Organic Catalog" - a shop aggregator (single repo: frontend + backend).
  Goal: show 10 products from each of two external shops (karashynyard.com.ua, osio-organic.com.ua)
  in one catalog; users add products to a basket and update/delete basket items.
  Stack: TypeScript, pnpm workspace (apps/web, apps/api), Node 22.
  Testing: Vitest for unit/contract tests, Playwright for e2e; every task must be verified by a test or command.
  Conventions: conventional commits; kebab-case capability names (product-catalog, basket, shop-import).
  Practices to prove: SDD (OpenSpec), AGENTS.md context rules, loop engineering, maker != checker review pass.

rules:
  proposal:
    - Keep proposals under 500 words
    - Always include a "Non-goals" subsection under Impact
  specs:
    - Every requirement uses SHALL; every scenario uses WHEN/THEN bullets
    - Reference the external shop by name in scenarios that depend on it
  design:
    - Document which data is scraped vs seeded and how it is refreshed
  tasks:
    - Each task names the test or command that verifies it
    - Break tasks into chunks of max 2 hours

operations:
  apply:
    guidance:
      - Run the focused test for the task before the full suite
      - Mark a task [x] only after its verification passes
  archive:
    guidance:
      - Summarize which specs were merged before finishing

created: 2026-10-04            # YYYY-MM-DD, written by `new change`

Claude Code invocation form is `/opsx:<workflow>` (namespaced command files .claude/commands/opsx/<workflow>.md); each also exists as an auto-triggerable skill .claude/skills/openspec-<name>/SKILL.md. All are generated by `openspec init --tools claude` / `openspec update`. Other tools use `/opsx-<workflow>` (Cursor, Copilot) or `/openspec-<workflow>` (skills-only tools) - irrelevant for Claude Code.

CORE profile (installed by default - 6 commands, verified):
- /opsx:propose <name-or-description>  (skill openspec-propose) - "Propose a new change - create it and generate all artifacts in one step". Runs `openspec context --json`, derives kebab-case name, `openspec new change "<name>"`, then for each artifact `openspec instructions <artifact> --change "<name>" --json` and writes proposal.md -> specs/<cap>/spec.md -> design.md -> tasks.md, re-checking `openspec status --change "<name>" --json`. PLANNING ONLY: it explicitly refuses to touch project code and stops after artifacts; you must then run /opsx:apply in a new message.
- /opsx:explore [topic]  (openspec-explore) - "Enter explore mode - think through ideas, investigate problems, clarify requirements". Read-only thinking partner; optional before propose.
- /opsx:apply [change-name]  (openspec-apply-change) - "Implement tasks from an OpenSpec change". This IS the "implement" step (there is no /opsx:implement). Runs `openspec status --change X --json` and `openspec instructions apply --change X --json`, works through tasks.md, flips `- [ ]` to `- [x]` immediately after each task passes its verification, pauses on blockers. Auto-selects the change if only one is active.
- /opsx:update [change-name]  (openspec-update-change) - "Update a change - revise existing planning artifacts and keep them coherent". Drafts edits to proposal/specs/design/tasks, applies after your confirmation, never edits code. (Not to be confused with CLI `openspec update`, which regenerates .claude/ files.)
- /opsx:sync [change-name]  (openspec-sync-specs) - "Sync delta specs from a change to main specs". AGENT-DRIVEN merge: the agent reads each delta and edits openspec/specs/<cap>/spec.md directly (can add one scenario without rewriting the requirement), creates missing main specs from ADDED, then runs `openspec validate --specs`. Use when you want main specs updated before/without archiving.
- /opsx:archive [change-name]  (openspec-archive-change) - "Archive a completed change". Checks `openspec status --change X --json` completeness and task progress, loads `openspec instructions archive --change X --json` (context + operationGuidance), offers to run the /opsx:sync workflow inline for unsynced deltas (in 1.13.1 it delegates to the sync skill; 1.14.0 merges itself), then moves the change dir to openspec/changes/archive/YYYY-MM-DD-<name>/ (same naming rule as the CLI). The pure-CLI equivalent that does a programmatic merge is `openspec archive <name> --yes`.

EXPANDED workflows (available in 1.13.1 but NOT installed until you set profile=custom + workflows list, see init; verified they then appear as /opsx:* files):
- /opsx:new <name>  (openspec-new-change) - "Start a new change using the experimental artifact workflow" - scaffolds the change dir only (= `openspec new change`), no artifacts.
- /opsx:continue [name]  (openspec-continue-change) - "Continue working on a change - create the next artifact" - one artifact per invocation following the dependency graph; review between steps.
- /opsx:ff [name]  (openspec-ff-change) - "Create a change and generate all artifacts needed for implementation in one go" - fast-forward; functionally close to propose but starts from an existing /opsx:new change or a name.
- /opsx:verify [name]  (openspec-verify-change) - "Verify implementation matches change artifacts before archiving" - checks completeness (tasks done, requirements implemented, scenarios tested), correctness, coherence; reports gaps. Good "checker" pass for maker != checker.
- /opsx:bulk-archive  (openspec-bulk-archive-change) - "Archive multiple completed changes at once", resolving cross-change spec conflicts.
- /opsx:onboard  (openspec-onboard) - "Guided onboarding - walk through a complete OpenSpec workflow cycle with narration".

Typical loop for this project: /opsx:explore (optional) -> /opsx:propose "<idea>" -> review openspec/changes/<id>/* + `openspec validate <id> --strict` -> /opsx:apply <id> -> (optional /opsx:verify <id> if enabled) -> /opsx:archive <id> (or `openspec archive <id> --yes`). The user asked for "propose, implement, archive": implement = /opsx:apply.

DEPRECATED / LEGACY (do not use; not generated by 1.13.1): `/openspec:proposal`, `/openspec:apply`, `/openspec:archive` (old all-at-once commands in .claude/commands/openspec/, plus the `<!-- OPENSPEC:START -->` block in root AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md and openspec/AGENTS.md, openspec/project.md). `openspec init --force` / `openspec update` delete the OpenSpec-written legacy command files and strip the markers. Also deprecated CLI: `openspec change list` (use `openspec list`), `--requirements-only` (use `--deltas-only`). Tags in command frontmatter still say "experimental" for the OPSX workflow - that is the current, recommended path per the docs.

toolu_015ngDeesbxhifYuRMBFAzkP.specFormat:
Parser facts (dist/core/parsers + validation, 1.13.1): headings are matched case-insensitively; section headers are `##`, requirements `### Requirement: <name>`, scenarios MUST be `#### Scenario: <name>` (exactly 4 hashes - 3 hashes or bullet-only scenarios "fail silently" / are not counted); scenario bodies are bullet lines `- **WHEN** ...` / `- **THEN** ...` (and `- **AND** ...`, `- **GIVEN**` accepted as free text); requirement body SHOULD contain the English keyword SHALL or MUST (missing keyword = WARNING, which FAILS under --strict); every ADDED/MODIFIED requirement needs >= 1 scenario (ERROR); requirement text > 500 chars = INFO; delta spec must live at specs/<capability-path>/spec.md (a file at specs/spec.md is an ERROR and ignored by archive); capability path segments kebab-case.

A) MAIN spec (openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md) - what archive produces/maintains; passes `openspec validate --all --strict` (verified):

# product-catalog Specification

## Purpose
Provides a single read-only catalog that aggregates products from several integrated organic shops.

## Requirements

### Requirement: Catalog lists aggregated products
The system SHALL return a list of products aggregated from all integrated shops, each with name, price, image and source shop.

#### Scenario: Catalog is requested
- **WHEN** a client requests `GET /api/products`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array of products from every integrated shop

Rules: required headers "## Purpose" and "## Requirements"; Purpose >= 50 chars (shorter = WARNING = strict fail), not a TBD/TODO placeholder; at least one requirement; main specs must NEVER contain ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED/RENAMED headers.

B) DELTA spec (openspec/changes/<id>/specs/<capability-path>/spec.md) - minimal NEW-capability delta that passed `openspec validate <id> --strict` and archived cleanly (verified):

# Spec Delta

## Purpose

Provides a single read-only catalog that aggregates products from several integrated organic shops.

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Catalog lists aggregated products
The system SHALL return a list of products aggregated from all integrated shops, each with name, price, image and source shop.

#### Scenario: Catalog is requested
- **WHEN** a client requests `GET /api/products`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array of products from every integrated shop

C) Delta for an EXISTING capability (no ## Purpose - it is ignored for existing specs) using MODIFIED (verified; archive replaced the requirement block and kept both scenarios):

# Spec Delta

## MODIFIED Requirements

### Requirement: Catalog lists aggregated products
The system SHALL return a list of products aggregated from all integrated shops, each with a stable id, name, price, image and source shop.

#### Scenario: Catalog is requested
- **WHEN** a client requests `GET /api/products`
- **THEN** the response is HTTP 200 with a JSON array of products from every integrated shop

#### Scenario: Product ids are stable
- **WHEN** the catalog is requested twice
- **THEN** every product keeps the same id across both responses

D) All delta section forms (full template from the shipped sync skill):

## ADDED Requirements          # new requirements; appended to main spec
## MODIFIED Requirements       # header must match an existing `### Requirement:` name (whitespace-insensitive); MUST carry the FULL block (text + every surviving scenario) - a MODIFIED that drops a scenario the main spec has is rejected by validate and archive ("scenario-loss guard"); the whole block is replaced
## REMOVED Requirements        # only the header is needed to delete: `### Requirement: Deprecated Feature`; schema instruction says also add `**Reason**: ...` and `**Migration**: ...` lines (good practice; validator only parses names - enforcement unconfirmed)
## RENAMED Requirements        # bullet pairs: `- FROM: `### Requirement: Old Name`` then `- TO: `### Requirement: New Name``; must be complete pairs

Delta validation rules (validate / --strict): >= 1 delta across the change unless .openspec.yaml has skip_specs: true; no duplicate requirement names within a section; no cross-section conflicts (same name in ADDED+REMOVED, MODIFIED+ADDED, MODIFIED+REMOVED, RENAMED+REMOVED, RENAMED TO vs ADDED); MODIFIED must use the new name after a RENAME; delta description (first requirement sentence) >= 10 chars (WARNING); ADDED/MODIFIED section with zero parsed requirements (WARNING); > 10 deltas per change ("Consider splitting", level unconfirmed); requirements written outside any delta section are warned with line numbers and ignored. `--strict` = valid only when errors == 0 AND warnings == 0 (dist/core/validation/validator.js createReport). Archive merge semantics: ADDED -> appended under ## Requirements; MODIFIED -> block replaced by name; REMOVED -> block deleted (if it empties the spec, archive aborts unless retire_capabilities: true, which then deletes the main spec); RENAMED -> header renamed; new capability -> file created with "# <cap> Specification" + Purpose from delta + "## Requirements".
